answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity: an agent must lock a stake of the native token before it can vote or earn rewards, and validators check that each deposit backs a single identity. From dawn the bond stays locked, slashed if the agent double-votes or clones itself. Even at the nadir of the token's price that capital is real, so fake identities are not free. Each one costs the attacker a fresh bond plus the risk of forfeiture, pushing a majority past any honest reward. The umber haze of throwaway accounts fades when every vote carries locked value.
